title: A rational Diophantine septuple
credit: Classical (Diophantus, Fermat, Euler); modern formulation and record constructions by Dujella, Gibbs, Kazalicki, Mikić, Szikszai
premise_risks: Listed on Epoch FrontierMath Open Problems, so actively targeted by AI search efforts; could be found by computation
Expected answer unknown; if no septuple exists, a proof is far beyond current methods (needs bounds on rational points of general-type varieties)
plain: A rational Diophantine m-tuple is a set of m distinct nonzero rational numbers such that the product of any two of them, plus 1, is a square of a rational number. Infinitely many such sets of size 6 are known, but nobody knows whether a set of size 7 exists. Find one, or prove that none exists.
math: Decide whether there exist seven distinct $a_1,\dots,a_7\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0\}$ such that $a_ia_j+1$ is the square of a rational number for all $1\le i<j\le7$.
